title: MV [SOLVED] Need help with an adjustment to a Jump skill

posts.author: Ian_39
posts.body:
Hello, all! I’m having a bit of trouble with a custom passive state I’ve made using Yanfly’s Buffs and States Core, and was hoping someone might be able to give me some insight.
The idea is that the character has a passive state called Cowardice, and it adds 1 stack at the start of their turn up to a max of 10. It debuffs their DEF, EVA, and HIT a certain percentage per stack. The character can use the Jump skill, and the number of turns they stay in the air is equal to their total Cowardice stacks +1 (min 2 turns, max 11 turns). The Cowardice stack also multiplies the damage they deal to the target (DMG Multiplier = 0.5 + (Cowardice Stacks / 3)).
So far, the debuffs and damage multiplier work exactly how I want. The issue I’m having is in tying the number of turns the Jump state lasts to the total number of Cowardice stacks. I assume that the problem is coming from how the Jump state is being applied, since it is applied via the Action Sequence rather than RPG Maker MV’s default method.
I figure the best work around would be to create another state called “Apply Jump” that simply forces the user to use a nameless skill that applies Jump to the user and then removes the “Apply Jump” state (similar to how the Jump state forces the user to use the Dive skill to attack). My concern is that I’m not certain how that will affect the target for the Dive skill, because Jump forces the user to use Dive against their last target.
If I use this method, would the last target be the user? Or would it still be the enemy selected when they used the Jump skill?
For reference, I’m building this off of Yanfly’s tutorial for the Jump skill, linked below:
http://www.yanfly.moe/wiki/Jump_(MV_Plugin_Tips_%26_Tricks)

posts.author: ATT_Turan
Ian_39
posts.body:
ATT_Turan said:
All you should need to do is give your Jump state a Custom Apply Effect that does
Code:
user._stateTurns[stateId] = user.getStateCounter(12);
Click to expand...
It works perfectly! Thank you!
